**r7 adjacent-pad short table (finding tabx-tap-pad-adjacency-unanalysed, H.23(g)).** The pad gap is 2.54 - 1.50 = 1.04 mm. Each
row assumes one hand-solder bridge or one stray strand across that gap. The 6 x 4 grid has 38 orthogonal pairs. Seven of them
contain a spare position and cannot bridge: (50.80, 61.48)-(53.34, 61.48), (53.34, 61.48)-(55.88, 61.48), (50.80, 66.56)-(53.34, 66.56),
(53.34, 66.56)-(55.88, 66.56), (53.34, 58.94)-(53.34, 61.48), (53.34, 61.48)-(53.34, 64.02) and (53.34, 64.02)-(53.34, 66.56). The
other 31 pairs and the residual-row pairs are listed below. A **push-pull pad** is a pad whose tap wire runs straight to a Teensy
output pin. The CR series resistors of A.4 sit behind the pads, so they do not limit a bridge between two tap wires. The
contention figures take about 40 ohm per i.MX output driver (ASSUMPTION, not measured). The T-F-12 tap-to-tap check detects
every row before the first power-up; the last column names the detector in service.

Two rows lie outside the H.23(g) exclusion set but carry the hazard class that the set excludes. F05-F12 ties two push-pull
outputs on an RT1987 EN net, as an EN-EN pair does. F07-F12 lets a push-pull output sink the unlimited Teensy 3V3, as a GND
neighbour of F07 does. Neither row has a detector in service. Both stand only behind the T-F-12 tap-to-tap check until a
ruling. The proposed closure adds one exclusion (no EN tap and no F07 beside a push-pull pad: T10, T11 or T21) and re-runs
H.23(g), TODO(calc: r7_calc.py H.23(g) with the added exclusion). One candidate swaps F12 (T11) and F24, so that only the
unfitted F24 option sits beside F05 and F07.
